label: WRONG
reason: The 44 members are exactly the exported send* functions of the top-level service files (auth-email-service.ts, organization-email-service.ts, workflow-email-service.ts, email-manager.ts), but the two exempted outliers are exported helpers in email-manager.ts:62/67 (an org-settings stub and a skip predicate), neither the definition nor an aggregator, so by R1 they count as legit (0 of 2), and the ./** scope also covers lib helpers such as getFormattedDate and sanitizeDisplayName that are not senders. Hesitated with ACCEPT, since the rule's own wording carves out companion helpers and send* naming of senders is a deliberate scheme.

label: ACCEPT
reason: Every other route file wraps its handler in defaultResponderForAppDir (error-to-JSON mapping, Sentry, perf marks), even equally trivial ones like version/route.ts and geolocation/route.ts, so the bare csrf and ip GETs and video/recording's hand-rolled try/catch are drift worth a look; only og/image is legitimately different (export runtime = 'edge', while the responder pulls in node:perf_hooks via perfObserver). That makes 3 of 4 look, and nothing in biome.json enforces it.

label: ACCEPT
reason: Templates extend BaseEmail directly (account-verify-email.ts, feedback-email.ts) or via another template (attendee-cancelled-email.ts), and the only exempt member is the definition in _base-email.ts, which holds the kill switch, test-mode capture and address sanitizing. The types do not force this: the protected members only bite when a template is passed through a service file's sendEmail(prepare: () => BaseEmail), while BookingAttendeesRemoveService.ts:126-127 instantiates a template and calls .sendEmail() directly, so a new class not extending BaseEmail could compile and skip the kill switch. A required base class: ACCEPT.
